body.x: My Pocket Farm (CEO Seong Kyoon Je) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

The company specializes in precision agriculture, leveraging AI and sensor technology to revolutionize high-value crop cultivation. Its smart farming solution integrates environmental conditions and metabolic data analysis to optimize farming processes and enhance efficiency. Designed to track ecological variables and real-time crop metabolic activity, the system ensures optimal growth environments, meeting the demands of research institutions and high-value crop markets.

At CES 2025, My Pocket Farm will introduce its namesake smart farming solution, showcasing its benefits and technological distinctions to a global audience. The solution collects and analyzes crop data in real time using multiple sensors and AI models. It enables refined crop management beyond traditional data collection methods by precisely monitoring internal metabolic changes alongside external environmental factors.

This data-driven approach boosts agricultural productivity, supports efficient resource use, and promotes eco-friendly farming practices. With support from a government-sponsored startup package program, My Pocket Farm continues to refine its solution and aims to expand into domestic and international markets.

A company representative stated that participation in CES 2025 reflects a strategic effort to accelerate the growth of high-value crops like hemp and bio-materials. The company seeks research collaborators for crop growth acceleration and high-purity substance synthesis studies. Additionally, it aims to connect with suppliers of essential cultivation materials and technology while building networks to share marketing strategies and investment opportunities.

The representative added that while the company is still in its early growth stage, it sees CES as an opportunity to make significant progress toward entering the North American market. Given the region's large agricultural market and high acceptance of smart farming technologies, My Pocket Farm expects its solutions to demonstrate substantial value. The company also plans to leverage its success in the U.S. to expand its network and explore export opportunities in other regions.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
